# Role: remote-builder

Runs a build, a codegen or a test suite somewhere other than the machine you are
typing on — a container, or a box with the toolchain and the cores — and brings
back an artifact you can say something true about.

**Use it when** the toolchain is absent locally, the download would be
expensive, the arch is wrong, or the run needs cores nothing else is using.

**Do not use it** for benchmarks handed to a subagent: those are serial,
foreground work on pinned cores
([`../skills/freeunit-benchmark/SKILL.md`](../../skills/freeunit-benchmark/SKILL.md)).

Hosts are roles (`build`, `alpine`, `lab`), resolved by `tools/hosts` from the
gitignored lab env file `run/lab.env`; see [`../docs/host-roles.md`](../../docs/host-roles.md).
No host name appears in committed content. `tools/unit-build -H build` takes the role;
`tools/hosts list` shows what it resolves to.

## Brief

> Build `<target>` from `<repo>` at `<explicit sha>` on the `<role>` host (`tools/hosts ssh <role>`).
> Pin the platform explicitly (`docker run --platform linux/amd64 …`) — never let
> the daemon resolve the arch by ambient default. Run the container as
> `--user "$(id -u):$(id -g)"` and mount the package/registry caches from the
> host. Read every version pin from the server repo (the generator version, the
> MSRV, the wasmtime/njs pins) rather than restating one; quote where you read
> it. Report the exact command, the pins you read and from which file, the
> artifact path, and `tools/mirror-check.sh` output for anything you synced
> back. If a toolchain looks absent, source its env first and re-check before
> reporting it missing.

## Output

```
Host/image: <image@pinned tag>, --platform <arch>
Command:    <the exact command, copy-pasteable>
Pins read:  <name>=<value> from <file:line>            (repeat)
Artifact:   <path> (<size>, <sha256>)
Fidelity:   tools/mirror-check.sh … → missing=0 differ=0 unwritable=0
Could not verify: <…>
```

## How this role fails

**An unanchored rsync exclude eats committed sources.** `--exclude 'build/'`
matches at *every* depth, so a sync meant to skip the build directory also
dropped `tools/unitctl/build/package.mk` and, by the same mechanism,
`unit-openapi/src/apis/error.rs` — both tracked files whose directory merely
looks like an artifact directory. The remote build then failed for a reason
unrelated to the code. Anchor artifact excludes to the tree root:
`--exclude '/build/'`. Then prove it: `tools/mirror-check.sh <src> <dest>`
reports every tracked file the copy is missing. One line reproduces the
difference — a pattern with no internal slash is matched against the basename at
every depth:

```bash
mkdir -p s/build s/tools/x/build && touch s/build/a s/tools/x/build/keep.mk
rsync -a --exclude 'build/'  s/ d1/   # d1 has empty dirs — keep.mk is gone
rsync -a --exclude '/build/' s/ d2/   # d2 has tools/x/build/keep.mk
```

**The container writes as root and the next sync cannot replace what it left.**
The mechanism is not the one you would guess, and guessing it wrong sends you
looking at file modes: a root-owned `0644` *file* does not block `rsync` at all
— it writes a temp file alongside and renames over the target, taking ownership.
What blocks it is a *directory* owned by root, where `mkstemp` fails with
`Permission denied (13)`, and the errors read as transient while the tree keeps
stale content. Run with `--user "$(id -u):$(id -g)"`; `mirror-check.sh` flags
the directories as `UNWRITABLE`.

The same happens with `test/**/__pycache__` after a container ran pytest in
the synced tree: `rsync --delete` cannot remove the root-owned directories
and exits 23. `tools/unit-build` excludes `__pycache__` and aborts on any
rsync error. To clean a tree that is already poisoned:

```bash
ssh <host> 'docker run --rm -v <remote-root>/<tree>:/src alpine \
    sh -c "find /src -name __pycache__ -type d -exec rm -rf {} +"'
```

`<remote-root>` is `BUILD_ROOT` from the lab env file (`tools/hosts root build`).

**A second run on the same tree reads the first run's artifacts.**
`tools/unit-build` runs a remote build in the tmux session
`unitbuild-<basename of -s>`. It now refuses to start while that session
exists. Before, it rsynced over the running build and then failed at
`tmux new-session` with `duplicate session`. A caller that polled for "done"
then read a stale `build/tests`. Judge a run with
`tools/unit-build -t remote -H <host> -s <tree> verify` after the session
ends. It prints `build/tests` with its mtime (`STALE` when older than the
run), a fresh `./build/tests` exit code, the hook gate's exit code and last
line, the `warning:` count of the run's log, and the run's PASSED/FAILED
line.

**A toolchain is reported missing when it is installed.** `rustc` is not on a
non-interactive ssh PATH even where rustup installed it: `ssh <host> 'rustc
--version'` says "command not found" next to a working 1.98.0. Source the env
(`. "$HOME/.cargo/env"`) before concluding anything about what a box has.

**The pull resolves the wrong architecture.** Always pass `--platform`
explicitly; a box that also builds other arches will hand you an image you did
not ask for, and the failure appears much later as an unexplained illegal
instruction.

**A green build reflects hand repair, not the canonical path.** A generated
client compiled only after a subagent hand-patched 17 files; the container run
of the same target needed none of them. Before trusting any "it builds on
toolchain X", check the agent's edit footprint:
`git status --porcelain --ignored=matching <subtree>`.

## Procedure: prove which generated types a spec change moved

Diffing a spec tells you what you wrote; it cannot tell you what the generator
emits. Generate twice — at the base commit and at your head — with the *same*
pinned image, and diff the two model trees:

```bash
for rev in <base-sha> <head-sha>; do
    git worktree add --detach /tmp/gen-$rev $rev
    docker run --rm --platform linux/amd64 \
        --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" -v /tmp/gen-$rev:/w -w /w \
        <generator image, version read from the repo's own makefile> \
        generate --input-spec <spec> --config <config> --output <out> ...
done
diff -ru /tmp/gen-<base-sha>/<out>/src/models /tmp/gen-<head-sha>/<out>/src/models
```

Generating once and diffing against an *older* checked-in generation confounds
your change with everything that landed in between — that happened on
2026-08-29 and produced a wrong first answer. Two things to expect: regeneration
reverts hand-fixes in the crate manifest, and it writes an untracked
`.openapi-generator/` directory. Revert both before committing.
